messages:
maria: Hey team — our staging service started getting 401 invalid_api_key from the Redwood hosted endpoint around 09:13 UTC. Works from my laptop, fails from the pod. Posting repro and headers below.

maria: Repro (from pod):
```bash
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Token AbCd+EfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUvWxY123456" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```

maria: Response: 401 and body `\{"error":"invalid_api_key"\}`. Headers we see in envoy access log: `Authorization: Token AbCd+EfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUvWxY123456`

support-bot: @devon assigned to thread (auto-assign)

devon: Thanks — can you try two quick checks: 1) show the raw request headers captured by the pod (kubectl logs or tcpdump) and 2) try the same curl locally but switch the scheme to Bearer or send as x-api-key.

maria: Pasted extracted header from pod-side tcpdump (base64 masked):
```
Authorization: Token AbCd+EfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUvWxY123456
User-Agent: my-proxy/1.2
```

maria: Local curl that works (on my laptop):
```bash
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer AbCd+EfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUvWxY123456" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```

devon: Ah — we're expecting either `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or the `x-api-key: <key>` header. The `Token` auth scheme isn't recognized by our API, so the request is rejected as invalid key. Two options: make the proxy rewrite the header to `Bearer` or forward the key in `x-api-key`. Can you try one of those to confirm?

maria: Our proxy is a third-party auth proxy that maps their internal token into an outgoing `Authorization: Token ...` header by default. I can change the template but wanted to confirm Redwood can't accept `Token` as an alias.

devon: Correct — we don't accept `Token` as equivalent. We intentionally only accept `Bearer` and `x-api-key` to avoid ambiguous parsing. If you can't change the proxy easily, you can add a tiny Lua/Envoy header rewrite rule or set an upstream transform to swap `Token ` -> `Bearer `. Example Envoy header transform snippet (quick):
```yaml
request_headers_to_add:
  - header:
      key: Authorization
      value: "%REQ(Authorization)%"
  # use a Lua filter to replace scheme if needed — can share snippet if you want
```

maria: I tried updating the proxy template to `Authorization: Bearer {{.token}}` and retried from the pod: got 200! 🎉

maria: Follow-up — weirdly we also saw a few failed requests earlier even after switch; logs showed keys with plus signs replaced by spaces e.g. header value became `AbCd EfGh...` (space). That was still 401. Any thoughts?

devon: Plus signs becoming spaces usually means the header got url-decoded somewhere (plus decodes to space in x-www-form-urlencoded contexts). If any component treats the header value as form-encoded or does an extra decode pass, `+` can be turned into a space which corrupts the key. Quick check: can you grep your proxy logs for a raw hex dump of the header byte sequence? If there's `0x2b` vs `0x20` you'll confirm it.

maria: Confirmed — our proxy had a legacy step that url-decodes certain tokens before forwarding; it converted `+` to ` `. After disabling that decode the key was preserved and requests succeeded.

devon: Great — summary/next steps: 1) Proxy must forward credentials without changing/decoding them or rewrite scheme to Bearer, 2) You can rotate the key if you suspect it was exposed while corrupted, 3) Prefer `x-api-key` header if you want to avoid scheme parsing. I'll mark this thread resolved but ping if you hit anything else.

maria: Thanks @devon — fixing the proxy decode + switching to `Authorization: Bearer` solved it. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
